title: E0 Toolchain: the workspace must install, build, and be proven by CI
description:
Prerequisite phase discovered by the 2026-08-14 architecture review. E1's own exit criteria ('bun run check green in contracts and runtime') CANNOT currently pass, because the workspace does not install on any machine but the one it was authored on.

Evidence (measured 2026-08-14):
- video-pipeline-runtime/node_modules/@video-studio/workspace-contracts/* are absolute symlinks into /Users/alcibiade/... (a different user's home). Every file in the linked package is a dangling link.
- Consequence: 20 of 28 runtime test FILES fail at import with: Cannot find package '@video-studio/workspace-contracts/src/vocabulary.mjs'. Only 5 of 103 tests are genuine assertion failures; the rest never ran.
- video-workspace-contracts/package.json declares no main, no exports, no files.
- There is no root package.json, no workspace, no Makefile, no install script.
- CI exists in 1 of 11 modules (qwen-tts-worker only). Nothing would have caught any of the above.

This epic must land before E1, or E1 cannot be verified.

Exit criteria: a fresh clone on a different machine runs one documented command and reaches green typecheck+test in every module; no absolute path outside the repo appears in any lockfile, symlink, or tracked file.

title: Secrets hygiene: rotate FAL_KEY (user), gitignore audit, env-only docs
description:
## Task
1. USER ACTION (not the agent): rotate the FAL_KEY — the old one lived in plaintext `.env` and was exposed in a review session. Mark the old key revoked in the fal dashboard.
2. Create root `.gitignore` (root is not a git repo yet — still useful if it becomes one): `.env`, `.gateway-token`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `library-legacy/` (decide: large media — likely exclude or leave untracked).
3. Audit every module's `.gitignore` covers `.env` and token files: `for m in */; do cat $m/.gitignore 2>/dev/null | grep -l ".env" >/dev/null || echo "$m missing .env ignore"; done` — fix misses.
4. Document in root README: secrets come from the environment (`FAL_KEY`, `AVG_GATEWAY_TOKEN`); `.env` is a local convenience loaded by the developer's shell, never committed, never read from library or /tmp paths.
5. `grep -rn "FAL_KEY" --include="*.ts" --include="*.py" . --exclude-dir=node_modules -l` — every hit must be an env read, not a file fallback.

## Acceptance
- Old key revoked (user confirms); no file-based secret fallback in code; all .gitignores cover secrets.

## References
- ADR-0030

title: Produce and validate Give Me Time pilot at quarter scale
description: Run the complete 8-stage wordless-rigged-short pipeline for wordless-comedy/give-me-time/the-run-up. Preserve the approved test style, author a 30–60 second full pilot at 270x480 quarter scale, synthesize speech-free audio, compose and review final media, and retain human approvals and QA evidence.
notes: Completed the 36-second first episode at 270x480/30fps. All 8 custom pipeline stages materialized and runtime status reports complete. Creative validation, muted readability, safety, continuity, browser playback, authored silence, H.264/AAC, and audio QA passed. Output measured -14.03 LUFS and -2.14 dBTP. Delivery QA remains intentionally unapproved only because quarter scale is not 1080x1920. Improved PVA two-pass loudness composition/context normalization, runtime provider-neutral artifact discovery, and gateway canonical QA/status/autopilot reporting.
close_reason: Quarter-scale full pilot produced and validated; only the intentional full-resolution delivery gate remains.

title: Add wordless 2D character-short pipeline and Give Me Time pilot
description: Create a new 9:16 family-shorts channel, the Give Me Time series, and one pilot episode. Extend PVA with generalized workspace-authoring and deterministic rigged-2D animation support, plus reusable series-local skills and validation.
acceptance_criteria: PVA can create channel/series/episode workspaces through tools; a generalized 9:16 rigged-vector pipeline is represented in the workspace; the new channel, series, and pilot episode are valid and discoverable; series-local skills define format, visual-comedy planning, vector authoring, sound cues, and QA; relevant tests and builds pass.
notes: Implemented canonical idempotent channel/series/episode authoring in pi-video-agent; added deterministic SVG rig renderer, nonverbal buzz synthesis, and frame-addressed multitrack composition; fixed PVA slash-command compatibility and .env config loading; fixed gateway support-directory discovery and inherited pipeline forwarding; created wordless-comedy/give-me-time/the-run-up with five local skills, an 8-stage resolved pipeline, canonical workspace contracts, and a rendered pipeline smoke test. PVA typecheck and all 100 tests pass. Gateway focused tests pass; baseline failures tracked separately.
close_reason: Channel, series, pilot scaffold, generalized PVA tools, local skills, pipeline validation, and smoke media completed.

title: Secure the Dyne software hybrid explainer pipeline in the series workspace
description: Promote the successful JaroMail v3 format into a series-local, versioned pipeline under library/dyne/software. Define explicit contracts and gates for separated Remotion infographic and VHS scenes, cue-addressable narration, measured timing/SRT, approved soundtrack mixing, composition, and QA. Add series-local skills and a deterministic validator so a less-capable model can execute the workflow with bounded decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Series pipeline selector resolves to a valid series-local pipeline; pipeline resolves without errors; local skills are discoverable; runbook defines exact artifact layout and invariants; deterministic validator accepts JaroMail v3 and rejects key structural mistakes; existing JaroMail remains the reference fixture.
close_reason: Locked dyne/software to dyne-software-hybrid-explainer@1.0.0 in the series workspace; added a 13-stage resolvable manifest, seven discoverable stage skills, explicit human gates, artifact/runbook contracts, a content-hashed lock file, an explicit-pipeline wrapper for the current gateway limitation, and positive/negative deterministic validation using JaroMail v3. Final check script passes.

title: Rebuild JaroMail as distinct infographic and VHS scenes with synced captions
description: Remove the infographic progress bar; redesign the episode so Remotion infographic chapters and regenerated VHS terminal demonstrations are separate scenes rather than overlays; rewrite and regenerate narration as needed; regenerate frame-accurate SRT captions; preserve the now-approved soundtrack behavior; produce and validate a new immutable render without fal.ai.
acceptance_criteria: No infographic progress bar; infographic and VHS content have distinct scene IDs and non-overlapping timeline ranges; VHS recordings are regenerated at delivery resolution; narration is regenerated from the revised script; SRT cues derive from measured narration segment durations and validate against the final duration; soundtrack behavior remains equivalent to approved v2; final 1080p30 render passes visual and audio QA.
close_reason: Rebuilt JaroMail v3 with the global infographic progress bar removed; seven regenerated Remotion scenes and three regenerated 1080p VHS scenes occupy distinct timeline ranges; rewrote and regenerated 28 cue-addressable Qwen narration segments; generated canonical, sidecar, and embedded captions from measured WAV durations with sub-millisecond validation; preserved the approved soundtrack mix; validated and published the 1080p30 output.

title: Revise JaroMail with VHS scenes and stronger dynamic music mix

Re-time narration with intentional pauses where the supplied music can rise, increase the general soundtrack level without masking speech, render a new immutable output, and validate visual/audio delivery. Also initialize and commit the completed remotion-infographic-renderer module as explicitly requested.
acceptance_criteria: The Remotion module has its own initial Git commit; JaroMail v2 visibly uses s4a/s4b/s5 VHS assets; narration has intentional pause intervals; music is generally louder and rises during those pauses while remaining ducked beneath speech; final 1080p30 output and QA report pass validation.
